source.original_text: For each natural n>=2, a real-valued total function u, center a and R>0, suppose an actual function v is harmonic near every point of the parent closed ball and agrees with u on that ball. In the explicit real closed-ball radial-polar specialization of the zero-flux use, one such extension can be retained before all radii: the same v remains harmonic and agrees on the parent ball, and for every0<r<=R its actual gradient paired with the unit sphere vector at a+r*zeta is integrable for the literal unnormalized polar measure of Euclidean volume and has integral zero. Original u is arbitrary outside the ball. This is the explicit same-witness/all-subradii specialization associated with the source two filled-ball uses, not full complex arbitrary-domain Eq1.3, geometric surface-law identification, annulus orientation or a mean-value theorem.

lean.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ)
    (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (R : ℝ) (hR : 0 < R)
    (hu : ∃ v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ,
      InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd v (Metric.closedBall a R) ∧
      Set.EqOn v u (Metric.closedBall a R)),
    let τ : MeasureTheory.Measure (Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1) :=
      (MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))).toSphere
    ∃ v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ,
      InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd v (Metric.closedBall a R) ∧
      Set.EqOn v u (Metric.closedBall a R) ∧
      ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r ≤ R →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ζ : Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1 =>
          inner ℝ (gradient v (a + r • ζ.1)) ζ.1) τ ∧
        (∫ ζ : Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1,
          inner ℝ (gradient v (a + r • ζ.1)) ζ.1 ∂τ) = 0
decoder_context: EuclideanSpace real (Fin n) has the standard real n-dimensional l2 norm and inner product; n is a natural number. Natural subtraction is truncated.
ContDiffAt real k f x for finite k means actual local continuous real differentiability of order k at x, on a neighborhood of x.

The volume measure is actual Lebesgue volume. Its toSphere law is the unnormalized polar measure on the unit-sphere subtype: for a measurable unit-sphere set S its measure is n times volume of the cone {r*zeta:0<r<1,zeta in S}. In dimension zero this law is zero.
Integrable means actual scalar L1 for the specified measure; IntegrableOn uses its restriction to the stated set. The integral is the real Bochner integral, whose equality alone does not assert L1.

gradient f is the Riesz representative of the actual real Fréchet derivative. HarmonicOnNhd f S means that at every x in S, f is locally C2 and its actual Euclidean Laplacian is zero on a neighborhood of x.

EqOn v u K means pointwise equality at every point of K. It gives no regularity of the total u outside K. An existential function outside a universal radius quantifier is one fixed function for all those radii.

reconstruction.text: For every natural number n >= 2, let E = R^n with its standard Euclidean norm and real inner product, and let S = {zeta in E : ||zeta|| = 1}. Let tau be the unnormalized polar measure on S induced by n-dimensional Lebesgue volume: for measurable A contained in S, tau(A) is n times the Lebesgue volume of {t zeta : 0 < t < 1, zeta in A}. For every function u : E -> R, center a in E, and real radius R > 0, set K = {x in E : ||x-a|| <= R}. Suppose there exists a function w : E -> R such that w is harmonic on a neighborhood of K and w(x) = u(x) for every x in K. Here harmonic on a neighborhood of K means that, at every point of K, the function is locally twice continuously real differentiable and its actual Euclidean Laplacian vanishes on a neighborhood of that point. Then there exists one function v : E -> R, harmonic on a neighborhood of K and equal to u at every point of K, such that for every real r with 0 < r <= R the scalar function zeta -> <gradient v(a + r zeta), zeta> belongs to L1(S,tau), and its real Bochner integral over S with respect to tau equals zero. The gradient is the Riesz representative of the actual real Frechet derivative. This one v is chosen before, and works simultaneously for, all these radii r. No regularity of u outside K is assumed or concluded, and the flux assertion concerns gradient v. The L1 assertion is a conclusion in addition to the zero integral equality.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Calculus.BallFlux
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Harmonic.Basic

/-!
Real closed-ball specialization of the zero-flux fact used in HFT1.4.
The one actual harmonic extension is retained at every positive subradius.
The differentiated function is that extension; the original total function is
arbitrary off the closed ball. The boundary law is literal volume.toSphere.
-/

open MeasureTheory Metric Set Filter
open scoped Topology RealInnerProductSpace

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Harmonic.SphericalFlux

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section

private theorem gradient_c1 {n : ℕ} (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ)
    (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (hv : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 v x) :
    ContDiffAt ℝ 1 (gradient v) x := by
  unfold gradient
  let L := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))).symm.toContinuousLinearEquiv
  exact L.contDiff.contDiffAt.comp x (hv.fderiv_right (m := 1) (by norm_num))

private theorem divergence_gradient {n : ℕ} (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ)
    (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (hv : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 v x) :
    Calculus.Divergence.coordinateDivergence (gradient v) x = Laplacian.laplacian v x := by
  have hgd := ((gradient_c1 v x hv).differentiableAt one_ne_zero).hasFDerivAt
  have hfd := ((hv.fderiv_right (m := 1) (by norm_num)).differentiableAt one_ne_zero).hasFDerivAt
  rw [Calculus.Divergence.coordinateDivergence_eq_sum_fderiv_apply_of_hasFDerivAt hgd,
    InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis v
      (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ)]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  let e := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)
  let π : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
    PiLp.proj (p := 2) (𝕜 := ℝ) (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ) i
  have hcomp : (fun y => (gradient v y) i) = fun y => fderiv ℝ v y e := by
    funext y
    change (gradient v y) i = fderiv ℝ v y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))
    rw [← inner_gradient_left, EuclideanSpace.inner_single_right]
    simp
  have hl : fderiv ℝ (fun y => (gradient v y) i) x e =
      (fderiv ℝ (gradient v) x e) i := by
    simpa [π, Function.comp_def] using congrArg (fun L : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ => L e)
      (π.hasFDerivAt.comp x hgd).fderiv
  have hr : fderiv ℝ (fun y => fderiv ℝ v y e) x e = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ v) x e e := by
    simpa using congrArg (fun L : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ => L e)
      (hfd.clm_apply (hasFDerivAt_const e x)).fderiv
  simp only [EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply, iteratedFDeriv_two_apply]
  change (fderiv ℝ (gradient v) x e) i = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ v) x e e
  rw [← hl, hcomp, hr]

-- The source standing dimension and parent-radius hypotheses are retained
-- literally even though the internal all-subradii argument is more general.
set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
/-- One source harmonic extension has integrable zero radial gradient flux at
all positive internal radii, including the parent boundary. -/
theorem harmonic_closedBall_zero_flux {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ)
    (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (R : ℝ) (hR : 0 < R)
    (hu : ∃ v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ,
      InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd v (Metric.closedBall a R) ∧
      Set.EqOn v u (Metric.closedBall a R)) :
    let τ : MeasureTheory.Measure (Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1) :=
      (MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))).toSphere
    ∃ v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ,
      InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd v (Metric.closedBall a R) ∧
      Set.EqOn v u (Metric.closedBall a R) ∧
      ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r ≤ R →
        MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ζ : Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1 =>
          inner ℝ (gradient v (a + r • ζ.1)) ζ.1) τ ∧
        (∫ ζ : Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1,
          inner ℝ (gradient v (a + r • ζ.1)) ζ.1 ∂τ) = 0 := by
  dsimp only
  obtain ⟨v, hv, hvu⟩ := hu
  refine ⟨v, hv, hvu, ?_⟩
  intro r hr hrR
  have hvsub : InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd v (closedBall a r) :=
    hv.mono (closedBall_subset_closedBall hrR)
  obtain ⟨_, hL1, hflux⟩ := Calculus.BallFlux.ball_flux_eq_integral_divergence
    (gradient v) a r hr (fun x hx => gradient_c1 v x (hvsub x hx).1)
  refine ⟨hL1, ?_⟩
  have hvol : (∫ x in ball a r, Calculus.Divergence.coordinateDivergence (gradient v) x) = 0 := by
    apply setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero
    intro x hx
    have hh := hvsub x (ball_subset_closedBall hx)
    rw [divergence_gradient v x hh.1]
    exact hh.2.eq_of_nhds
  rw [hvol] at hflux
  exact (mul_eq_zero.mp hflux.symm).resolve_left (pow_ne_zero _ hr.ne')

end
end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Harmonic.SphericalFlux

notation.text: One actual extension, the literal unnormalized polar unit-sphere measure, and any0<r<=R.

steps.title: Retain one actual extension
steps.text: Choose the extension supplied by closed-set harmonicity once. Restrict its neighborhood harmonicity to each smaller closed ball. Equality with the original function remains on the parent ball; no derivatives of the original off-ball representative are used.
steps.formula: v=u\text{ on }\overline B(a,R),\qquad 0<r\le R\Longrightarrow v\text{ harmonic near }\overline B(a,r).
steps.lean: harmonic_closedBall_zero_flux chooses v before introducing r and uses HarmonicOnNhd.mono.

steps.title: Identify actual gradient regularity and divergence
steps.text: Local C2 of the extension gives local C1 of its actual gradient through the Riesz map. In the Euclidean coordinate orthonormal basis, differentiating the actual gradient-component identity identifies its coordinate divergence with the actual Laplacian, which vanishes by harmonicity.
steps.formula: \nabla v\in C^1\text{ locally},\qquad\operatorname{div}(\nabla v)=\sum_i D_iD_i v=\Delta v=0.
steps.lean: gradient_c1 composes fderiv_right with the inverse Riesz equivalence. divergence_gradient differentiates the full component identity and evaluates the actual second Fréchet derivative in EuclideanSpace.basisFun.

steps.title: Apply ball flux and cancel the positive radius factor
steps.text: Apply the canonical ball-flux theorem to the extension gradient on each selected closed ball. It supplies actual scalar radial integrability. The volume integrand is zero; the positive radius power is nonzero, so the radial flux is zero. The same v supplies both the outer and inner source-use candidates.
steps.lean: The public proof calls ball_flux_eq_integral_divergence exactly once per r, retains its L1 conclusion, proves the volume integral zero and cancels the nonzero real radius power.
